WHY IT BELONGS

How it grows

A GROWING DESIGN VOCABULARY

Relationships, then landscape.

This generator samples hundreds of possible positions for each feature. It scores relationships, rejects overlaps and wet ground, and finds paths around the resulting footprints. It does not choose from saved ranch layouts.

Arrival anchors the homestead

The farmhouse prefers the entrance. The barn keeps working space between itself and the house. Their sizes remain fixed when the property changes.

Work has a center

Paddocks prefer the barn; the kitchen garden prefers the house. Optional features may be omitted if they cannot fit.

Water changes the answer

A pond or creek excludes building sites and interrupts routes. This version has no bridges; disconnected gates are reported.

A shared path network

Each gate searches for a route back to the growing network. Trees stay out of footprints, water and paths.

Character follows structure

Seasons recolor vegetation. Halloween adds pumpkins; whimsy adds a fairy ring; a harvest party hangs bunting at the farmhouse.

Simulation comes next

Animals are illustrative markers. Soil, drainage, grazing capacity, daily routines and weather are not simulated yet. Dimensions and relationships are preserved for later 3D work.
